opportunities.title: Reward system
opportunities.description:
Act as an expert full-stack developer and UI/UX designer. I am building a mobile-first web app (HTML/Tailwind CSS/JS) for 14-year-old boys to track household chores using a gaming-inspired theme (Valorant, Minecraft, Roblox aesthetic). 

Implement a Loss-Aversion Point Engine and Reward System using the following architecture:

1. DUAL-CURRENCY SYSTEM:
- XP (Experience Points): Earned ONLY through task completion. Permanent, cumulative, and never lost or docked. Drives overall level and gamer ranks (Unranked -> Iron -> Bronze -> Silver -> Gold -> Platinum -> Diamond -> Ascendant -> Radiant).
- Coins: Earnable spending currency used in the Rewards Shop.

2. LOSS-AVERSION & PENALTY MECHANICS:
- Missed / Failed Daily Tasks: Deduct Coins from the available balance (or forfeit the daily Coin multiplier) to leverage psychological loss aversion without touching permanent XP.
- Guardrail: Implement a minimum Coin threshold (e.g., balance cannot drop below zero) and clear penalty limits per task so kids don't feel a "sunk-cost demotivation" trap.
- Streak System: Track consecutive active days (🔥 Streak). Missing mandatory daily tasks resets or reduces the streak bonus multiplier.

3. REWARDS SHOP LIST (Structured Tiers):
Implement a customizable Rewards Shop with the following pre-loaded catalog:
- Tier 1 (Micro / Low Cost):
  * +30 Min Gaming Extension
  * One-Time Minor Chore Pass (Skip a task)
  * +30 Min Weekend Bedtime Buffer
- Tier 2 (Mid-Tier / Moderate Cost):
  * Choose Friday Night Dinner / Takeout
  * In-Game Currency / Cosmetic Allowance (Robux, V-Bucks, Valorant Points)

- Tier 3 (Boss-Level / High Cost):
  * Gaming Gear Upgrade (Headset, Mouse, Keyboard Cap)

4. PARENT CONTROL OVERRIDES:
- PIN-protected parent mode to approve completed high-value tasks, issue direct bonus/penalty Coin adjustments, and process reward redemptions.

opportunities.title: Bug: Trade Republic staking rewards and their tax are not imported
opportunities.description:
## Before you start (required)

### General checklist

- [x] I have removed personal / sensitive data from screenshots and logs
- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/we-promise/sure/issues?q=is:issue) and [discussions](https://github.com/we-promise/sure/discussions) to ensure this is not a duplicate issue

### How are you using Sure?

- [ ] I was a paying Maybe customer (hosted version)
- [ ] I use it on PikaPod, Umbrel or similar (VPS included)
- [x] I am a self-hosted user (local only)

### Self hoster checklist

- Self hosted app commit SHA (find in user menu): bdb280b3b
  - [x] I have confirmed that my app's commit is the latest version of Sure
- Where are you hosting?
  - [ ] Render
  - [ ] Docker Compose
  - [ ] Umbrel
  - [ ] PikaPod
  - [x] Other (please specify): TrueNAS SCALE app (Docker)

---

## Bug description

Trade Republic pays crypto staking rewards (Solana in my case) every week, and charges the tax on each reward to the cash account. The account statement lists every tax debit, for example:

```
Imposte · Staking Reward XF000SOL0012 Solana, quantity: 0.024461
```

Neither the reward nor the tax is on the Trade Republic timeline, so the sync cannot import them:

- **Crypto account:** the holding is correct, because it comes from the positions snapshot. The trades, though, add up to less than the position, since the reward coins have no trade. Cost basis and the holding's history miss them.
- **Cash account:** the current balance is correct, because it is anchored to Trade Republic's cash. The balance history, though, misses the small weekly tax debits, and drifts further from the statement each week before today.

On my account the statement has 46 weekly tax debits between November 2025 and October 2026. I read both timeline topics in full (`timelineTransactions` and `timelineActivityLog`, 61 pages). They contain no event for any reward or tax debit. Everything else on the statement reconciles line by line with what Sure imports from the timeline.

### To Reproduce

1. Hold a crypto asset with staking enabled at Trade Republic (for example Solana) for a few weeks.
2. Sync the Trade Republic connection.
3. Compare the crypto trades with the position quantity, and the cash account's history with the monthly statement.
4. See that the reward coins and the weekly "Staking Reward" tax debits are missing.

### Expected behavior

Staking rewards import as crypto buys at no cost, and their tax as a cash debit. If Trade Republic does not expose them outside the statement, the limitation should at least be documented, so users know why the crypto trades and the cash history differ from the statement.

opportunities.title: Prevent hosting cash rewards from replaying on reload or retry
opportunities.description:
## Summary

More Hosting Deals can pay cash from retryable Enabled handling. Its already-paid flag resets on load, and completion is marked only after the payment loop.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Enable More Hosting Deals with active ServerDeal items and receive the noon payout.
2. Save and reload during noon with the setting enabled.
3. Trace cold-start Enabled handling reaching payout again.
4. Exercise a failure after one credit but before the payment loop finishes.

Replay paths are verified in source. A Unity cash-balance reproduction has not been performed.

## Expected Behavior

A defined scheduled reward is not paid again merely because a save reloads or a catch-up handler is retried.

## Actual Behavior

The resettable Boolean permits a noon reload payout. A partially successful loop can repeat earlier transactions on another attempt.

## Environment

- Trainer: 5.6.0, develop 8064eb8f22ece9451561c4bff3aa10e534944691.
- Game target: current vendored Software Inc. Beta 1.8.42 assemblies.
- Deployment: Workshop source compilation and the DLL build.
- Review: source and decompiled native assembly; full Unity reproduction is identified separately below.

## Additional Context

Priority recommendation: P2.

Evidence: [payment](https://github.com/Trawis/T5B1/blob/8064eb8f22ece9451561c4bff3aa10e534944691/Trainer_v5/Trainer.Source/Features/MarketFeatures.cs#L35), [timing](https://github.com/Trawis/T5B1/blob/8064eb8f22ece9451561c4bff3aa10e534944691/Trainer_v5/Trainer.Source/Features/MarketFeatures.cs#L117), ResetGameState and Enabled/Hour registry entries. This contradicts the documented repeatability requirement of Enabled actions.

Suggested approach: separate deal catch-up from payout. The smallest option pays cash only through the scheduled hourly path; explicitly decide whether immediate noon-on-enable payment must remain. If preserving that catch-up, define saved cycle/payment identity, eligibility changes, migration for old saves and partial-failure semantics before coding. Do not assume one saved Boolean establishes exactly-once payment.

Acceptance conditions:
- Cover save before/after payout, noon reload, repeated reload, enable/disable at noon and the next normal noon.
- A partial attempt cannot repeat already-applied credits through retry.
- Preserve reward amounts and eligible deal types.
- Keep financial side effects out of retryable catch-up unless made demonstrably safe.
- Do not add a general transaction framework.
- Report focused tests and actual in-game validation separately.

Related: #266, #336, PR #418, #344. #246 concerned completed deal-type detection and is not this bug.

opportunities.description:
**Phase:** 3 (ROADMAP "Career milestones"; DESIGN 4.5)
**Depends on:** none (#86 reviews and #87 levels have merged)

## Goal
Goals that point the player somewhere ("serve 50 guests in a day", "reach 3.5 stars") and pay XP and cash when completed. This answers the friend's "nothing left to do" complaint.

## Do
- **`Milestone` Resource** in `data/milestones/`:
  - `id`, `title`, `description`, a condition type plus its target, `reward_xp`, `reward_cash`, `unlock_level`.
- **Condition types** (implement these, all evaluated at day close from existing data):
  - served in one day ≥ N
  - reputation ≥ X
  - profit in one day ≥ $N
  - total guests served ≥ N
  - owner level ≥ N
  - staff count ≥ N
  - days with no lost guests ≥ N in a row
- **About 12 starter milestones**, spread from day 1 to about day 25 of the current pacing, each with a fun title (adult audience, light humour).
- **When one completes at day close:** the reward goes into the ledger as a readable category ("Milestone bonus"), XP is added, and the evening report gets a "Milestone reached!" section near the top.
- **Saving:** completed milestones go in a registered save section, written at the morning autosave only (rule 9).
- **UI:** a Goals panel opened from the Menu, listing the active milestones (the next 3 unlocked) with progress bars, and the completed ones greyed out.

## Don't
- No new save point, no CI job, no raw ids (rules 9–11).

## Tests

opportunities.title: Peering: Lightning invoices for paid peering — issue, settle, renew, lapse
opportunities.description:
Part of the relay peering work in #931.

## Scope

The source (selling) side of paid peering, using nostream's existing payments processors — the same machinery as admission fees:

- When a configured peer with paid terms authenticates, the source relay issues a BOLT11 invoice for the amount/period from its advertised terms.
- Settlement is detected via the existing processor callbacks; on settlement the peer's feed access activates until the end of the paid period.
- Before expiry, the source offers a renewal invoice.
- If the period lapses unpaid, the feed is suspended — stored data and sync state are kept, so resuming is a payment, not a re-sync from zero.

## Acceptance

- A paid peering relationship completes end-to-end: authenticate → invoice → settlement → feed active for exactly the paid period.
- An unpaid lapse suspends the feed; paying the renewal resumes it without re-reconciliation.
- Invoice/settlement state per peer is recorded for the admin console.

opportunities.title: Paid plan: one-time purchase that unlocks paid features
opportunities.description:
A one-time purchase that unlocks the paid features in the extension. The platform will be a separate subscription; this license only covers the extension.

## Scope
- Buy once and unlock forever on that browser profile, with a way to restore the purchase on another browser or after reinstalling.
- `isPaid()` in `src/lib/plan.ts` is the single check every paid feature uses. It returns `false` today; this issue makes it real.
- A small "Upgrade" entry point in the panel and a clear list of what the paid plan includes.
- Works in both Chrome and Firefox builds.

## To decide (design spec before building)
- **Payment provider:** ExtensionPay (Stripe-backed, made for extensions, supports one-time payments) vs. Stripe Checkout plus a small license-check endpoint vs. license keys from Lemon Squeezy or Gumroad.
- **Offline behaviour:** cache the unlocked state so paid features keep working offline.
- **Price.**
- **Store rules:** the listing has to disclose paid features, and the Chrome Web Store's payment policies apply.

## Done when
- A test purchase unlocks paid features in both browsers, and restoring the purchase works on a second profile.
- Every paid feature issue checks `isPaid()`.
